source_title: Intel Investigation Notice: Levi & Korsinsky Notifies Investors of Pending Investigation Into Intel (INTC)
source_excerpt:
An investigation is examining what Intel's August 2026 SEC offering materials told investors about customer demand before the Company issued a below-consensus Q4 revenue outlook tied to PC-market softness.
NEW YORK , Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC ) shareholders are absorbing fresh losses after the stock fell on the Company's third-quarter 2026 earnings release. That release set fourth-quarter revenue guidance of approximately $15 billion to $16 billion, below Wall Street consensus of about $17 billion. If you bought Intel shares and that decline hit your portfolio, you may have legal rights. Investors who suffered losses are encouraged to tell us about your Intel losses as the investigation moves forward. You may also contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. via email at [email protected] or by telephone at (212) 363-7500.
The investigation centers on what Intel told investors in its filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. In offering materials filed with the SEC on August 10, 2026, the Company stated: "Customers continue to signal a strong and sustainable demand environment, driven by unprecedented investment in AI compute."
Less than three months later, management tied the below-consensus fourth-quarter outlook to continued softness in the PC market. The Company indicated that slowdown could last into at least the first half of 2027. The investigation concerns whether Intel's SEC disclosures adequately addressed PC-market conditions before that guidance reached investors.
Shareholders who lost money on INTC can request a free review of their Intel losses or call (212) 363-7500.
WHY LEVI & KORSINSKY -- Ranked in ISS Securities Class Action Services' Top 50 Report for seven consecutive years, Levi & Korsinsky, LLP is a nationally recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation. With a team of over 70 professionals, the firm has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for investors.
Frequently Asked Questions About the INTC Investigation
Q: Who is eligible to participate in the INTC investigation? A: Investors who purchased INTC stock or securities and suffered financial losses may be eligible. Eligibility is based on purchase date and documented losses -- not on whether you still hold the shares.
Q: Which statements are being investigated as potentially misleading? A: The investigation concerns whether Intel made materially false or misleading statements regarding its business conditions and revenue outlook. When the Company disclosed a fourth-quarter 2026 revenue forecast of approximately $15 billion to $16 billion -- below consensus -- the stock price declined.
Q: When did Intel allegedly mislead investors? A: The investigation concerns statements made before Intel's below-consensus fourth-quarter 2026 revenue outlook, including the Company's August 10, 2026 offering materials. The investigation is examining whether those statements caused investors to purchase securities at inflated prices.
Q: What do INTC investors need to do right now? A: Investors may gather brokerage records showing purchase dates, share quantities, and prices paid. Submit your information for a no-cost, no-obligation evaluation of your potential recovery . No immediate action is required to remain eligible to participate in the investigation.
Q: What documents do I need to participate? A: You need brokerage statements or trade confirmations showing purchase dates, share quantities, prices paid, and any later sale dates and prices.
Q: What if I already sold my INTC shares -- can I still recover losses? A: Yes. Eligibility is based on when you purchased, not whether you still hold the shares. Investors who bought INTC and sold at a loss may still participate in the investigation.
Q: Do I need to go to court or give testimony? A: No. Participating in the investigation does not require court appearances or depositions. If legal action is later pursued, the overwhelming majority of affected investors never appear in court either.
Q: What does it cost me to participate? A: There is no upfront cost to submit your information and find out whether you may be eligible to recover. If you choose to participate in any resulting action, these matters are generally handled on a contingency basis. Any attorneys' fees and expenses are subject to court approval.
